summary: Matane light, first lit 1 October 1873; the 1907 cylindrical tower, discontinued in 1951, and a keeper's house now used as a tourist office and museum by the city.

structures.type: wooden tower attached to keeper's house
cylindrical, painted red with red lantern
structures.material: reinforced concrete (Marine reports, LighthouseFriends, Quebec record); cast-iron panels covered with concrete (Quebec record); cast iron (Rowlett)
structures.note: 67 ft base to vane; put into service 10 November 1907
Built by A. Vezina for $4,750.21 (LighthouseFriends); Lire la Mer dates to 1910

access.note: City-owned; tower open in season. Hours differ: LighthouseFriends Tuesday to Saturday, early June to mid-October; Rowlett guided tours late June to late September, fee to climb.

events.note: Wooden tower attached to keeper's house; $2,860.56 (LighthouseFriends)
Moved close to the present site in summer 1884 by P. Jobin (Lire la Mer). LighthouseFriends dates the move to 1894. Year disputed.
Tower moved 100 feet inland because of erosion (LighthouseFriends). Year disputed (see 1884).
Changed in colour to bright red (Commissioner of Lights report)
New reinforced concrete tower (67 ft base to vane; cast-iron panels per the Quebec record) put into operation 10 November 1907; old light discontinued
Third-order Barbier, Bénard and Turenne lens, from Cape Norman, Newfoundland (LighthouseFriends)
Keeper's dwelling built by A. Vezina for $4,750.21 (LighthouseFriends); Lire la Mer dates the present house to 1910
Family memory printed by Lire la Mer: a ship identified as from Germany boarded by the RCMP off Matane days before the war began; not confirmed elsewhere

Quebec Airways plane crashed on river ice in December 1946; keeper lit the lamp to aid the search; survivors found north-west of Les Méchins (Lire la Mer); LighthouseFriends places the crash north-west of Les Mechins
Light discontinued 21 June 1951 when a breakwater light took over (Lire la Mer); 'vers 1951' (Quebec record); LighthouseFriends: deactivated in 1951
Light and lighthouse sold to the Historical Society of Matane for one dollar (LighthouseFriends); Rowlett says 1952
Transferred to the city of Matane (Rowlett); LighthouseFriends says ten years after 1951
Recognised as a heritage building (Quebec record, citing a 2014 city document)
Full renovation of the lighthouse and keeper's house (Lire la Mer)
Closed for restoration in spring 2019; reopened during the summer (Rowlett)
Tower painted white at some point between 1908 and 1917 (LighthouseFriends)

keepers.name: François-Xavier Dionne
keepers.note: First keeper; appointed 19 September 1873 at $200 a year (LighthouseFriends); suspended 16 May 1879 after several days' absence (Lire la Mer); spelled Francois Xavier Dionne in LighthouseFriends' roster.

keepers.name: Octave Desjardins
keepers.note: Appointed at 48 with a salary of $250 (Lire la Mer); removed his own outbuildings in 1899 (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Madame Banville
keepers.note: Ran the tower's telegraph for many years, per A. Gagnon's Monographie de Matane as quoted by Lire la Mer; first name and dates not given; relation to Joseph Banville not stated.

keepers.name: Joseph Banville
keepers.note: Named in the 1901 keepers' table as Banville, Joseph, Matane; retired 1 July 1926 aged 74 after 29 years and five months (Lire la Mer).

keepers.name: Jules-André-Octave Morin
keepers.note: Career soldier who fought in the First World War (Lire la Mer).

keepers.name: André Rioux
keepers.note: Reportedly a First World War veteran (Lire la Mer, 'ce serait').

keepers.name: Camille McKinnon
keepers.note: Last keeper. LighthouseFriends text says 1935 to 1951, its roster 1937 to 1951; Lire la Mer's heading says 1937 to 1957. Credited with lighting the lamp to help the 1946 search.

wrecks.vessel: Quebec Airways aircraft (not named in the sources)
wrecks.outcome: Crashed onto the river ice; survivors found north-west of Les Méchins; keeper lit the lamp to aid the search

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends dates the first tower's move 100 feet inland to 1894; Lire la Mer says it was moved in summer 1884 by P. Jobin. Not reconciled.
McKinnon: LighthouseFriends roster 1937-1951, its text 1935-1951, Lire la Mer heading 1937-1957. Morin and Rioux dates agree.
LighthouseFriends: sold to the Historical Society for one dollar in 1951, municipality ten years later. Rowlett: bought 1952, transferred to the city 1962.
LighthouseFriends: built 1909 by A. Vezina. Lire la Mer: 1910.
Lire la Mer places the crash on the ice a little east of Matane, with survivors found north-west of Les Méchins. LighthouseFriends places the crash north-west of Les Mechins.
LighthouseFriends: about one mile west of the Matane River. Lire la Mer: about three-quarters of a mile west.
LighthouseFriends: Tuesday to Saturday from early June to mid-October. Rowlett: guided tours late June to late September, fee to climb.

The Marine reports and LighthouseFriends say reinforced concrete. The Quebec record calls the tower reinforced concrete and also describes cast-iron panels bolted together and covered with concrete. Rowlett says cast iron. Not reconciled; the story gives the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: The 1946 Quebec Airways crash is in LighthouseFriends and Lire la Mer only; a Chronicling America search for Quebec Airways 1946 returned no hits, so it is unconfirmed by a newspaper. The 1939 German ship and the 1906 Montcalm log are the only atmosphere items beyond the keepers; the 1939 item is a family memory, which the story says. Captain Heppell is undated (Lire la Mer). The 1860 chief engineer's recommendation and the 1869 to 1875 loss figure rest on Lire la Mer, a local corporation's page, and were not found in the corpus. The 1884 move is from Lire la Mer only; LighthouseFriends gives 1894. The McKinnon years differ across LighthouseFriends (text 1935, roster 1937) and Lire la Mer (1957). The Quebec record gives construction as '1906 – 1907', calls the tower reinforced concrete and also describes cast-iron panels; Rowlett says cast iron. The Marine reports say reinforced concrete. Madame Banville (telegraph) is named by Lire la Mer quoting A. Gagnon's Monographie de Matane; no first name or dates are in the sources. Keeper dates for Desjardins and Banville rest on Lire la Mer and LighthouseFriends, which agree. The 1901 keepers table was checked on the page image: printed p. 144, scan p. 255, row 'Banville, Joseph | Matane | Feb. 1, 1897 | $250 00'. The story does not give the appointment date, because the cached OCR does not contain it. The 1904 Commissioner's colour change is recorded without a reason. The Quebec record's heritage date 2014-06-16 appears on the page, and its source is a 2014 city document; the story says 2014 only. The Montcalm log entry is 7 December 1905 (the log covers 3 December 1905 to 31 March 1906); an earlier draft wrote 1906.
